database_summary: E-commerce order dataset (SQLite) containing customers, sellers, orders, order items, payments, reviews, products, geolocation and product category translations. Mix of entity/dimension tables (customers, sellers, products), event/fact tables (orders, order_items, order_payments, order_reviews), and a large geolocation table mapping zip prefixes to coordinates. Many tables share natural keys like order_id, product_id, seller_id, customer_id and zip prefix. Dates are stored as text. Joins on order_id, product_id, seller_id and zip prefix are expected and can multiply rows when one-to-many relationships exist (e.g., orders -> order_items, orders -> payments).

accepted.name: orders_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  customer_id,
  order_status,
  order_purchase_timestamp,
  order_approved_at,
  order_delivered_carrier_date,
  order_delivered_customer_date,
  order_estimated_delivery_date,
  -- canonical datetime parsing: keep as TEXT but coalesce empty strings to NULL
  CASE WHEN trim(order_purchase_timestamp) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_purchase_timestamp END AS order_purchase_timestamp,
  CASE WHEN trim(order_approved_at) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_approved_at END AS order_approved_at,
  CASE WHEN trim(order_delivered_carrier_date) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_delivered_carrier_date END AS order_delivered_carrier_date,
  CASE WHEN trim(order_delivered_customer_date) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_delivered_customer_date END AS order_delivered_customer_date,
  CASE WHEN trim(order_estimated_delivery_date) = '' THEN NULL ELSE order_estimated_delivery_date END AS order_estimated_delivery_date
FROM olist_orders
accepted.description: Normalized orders table: one row per order with parsed timestamps and canonical status. Use as the cleaned orders dimension for joins and time-based analyses. | Use for: Time-to-delivery calculations per order; Order funnel (purchase -> approved -> delivered) analyses; Filtering orders by status or purchase date range

accepted.name: order_items_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  order_item_id,
  product_id,
  seller_id,
  shipping_limit_date,
  price,
  freight_value
FROM olist_order_items
accepted.description: Cleaned order items at the item grain: one row per order item preserving pricing and seller/product linkage. Use for revenue, item-level joins, and SKU/seller performance. | Use for: Revenue or freight aggregation at order/item level; Seller or product contribution to orders; Shipping SLA analysis using shipping_limit_date

accepted.name: payments_agg_per_order
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_lines_count,
  SUM(payment_value) AS payment_value_total,
  AVG(payment_installments) AS payment_installments_avg,
  -- dominant payment type by summed value per order using a deterministic tie-breaker (min payment_type)
  (SELECT payment_type
   FROM (
     SELECT payment_type, SUM(payment_value) AS v
     FROM olist_order_payments p2
     WHERE p2.order_id = p1.order_id
     GROUP BY payment_type
     ORDER BY v DESC, payment_type ASC
   ) LIMIT 1) AS payment_type
FROM olist_order_payments p1
GROUP BY order_id
accepted.description: Aggregated payment measures per order: total payment value, number of payment attempts, and dominant payment_type inferred by highest total value. Useful for order-level revenue and payment-method analyses. | Use for: Order revenue validation and reconciliation; Payment method mix and counts per order; Correlation of payment attempts with returns or delays

accepted.name: order_reviews_expanded
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.review_id,
  r.order_id,
  r.review_score,
  r.review_comment_title,
  r.review_comment_message,
  r.review_creation_date,
  r.review_answer_timestamp,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  o.order_status
FROM olist_order_reviews r
LEFT JOIN olist_orders o
  ON r.order_id = o.order_id
accepted.description: Order reviews joined to orders and customers: one row per review including order timestamps and customer identifiers for customer-level sentiment analysis. | Use for: Customer satisfaction and review trends over time; Linking reviews to order timing and status; Per-customer review frequency and scores

accepted.name: order_items_with_product
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.order_id,
  i.order_item_id,
  i.product_id,
  p.product_category_name,
  t.product_category_name_english,
  p.product_name_lenght,
  p.product_description_lenght,
  p.product_photos_qty,
  p.product_weight_g,
  p.product_length_cm,
  p.product_height_cm,
  p.product_width_cm,
  i.seller_id,
  i.price,
  i.freight_value,
  i.shipping_limit_date
FROM olist_order_items i
LEFT JOIN olist_products p
  ON i.product_id = p.product_id
LEFT JOIN product_category_name_translation t
  ON p.product_category_name = t.product_category_name
accepted.description: Order items enriched with product attributes and category name translation. One row per order item with product dimensions for SKU-level analytics and category rollups. | Use for: Category-level revenue and dimensions; Product weight/size impact on freight and delivery; Seller performance within product categories

accepted.name: seller_location
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.seller_id,
  s.seller_zip_code_prefix,
  s.seller_city,
  s.seller_state,
  AVG(g.geolocation_lat) AS geolocation_lat,
  AVG(g.geolocation_lng) AS geolocation_lng
FROM olist_sellers s
LEFT JOIN olist_geolocation g
  ON s.seller_zip_code_prefix = g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix
GROUP BY s.seller_id, s.seller_zip_code_prefix, s.seller_city, s.seller_state
accepted.description: Seller table joined to geolocation centroid per zip prefix: one row per seller with a representative latitude/longitude (avg) for the seller_zip_code_prefix. Useful for mapping and distance calculations. | Use for: Spatial analyses of sellers; Mapping seller distribution by state/city; Distance from seller to customer zip (when customer coords available)

accepted.name: customer_location
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_id,
  c.customer_unique_id,
  c.customer_zip_code_prefix,
  c.customer_city,
  c.customer_state,
  AVG(g.geolocation_lat) AS geolocation_lat,
  AVG(g.geolocation_lng) AS geolocation_lng
FROM olist_customers c
LEFT JOIN olist_geolocation g
  ON c.customer_zip_code_prefix = g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_unique_id, c.customer_zip_code_prefix, c.customer_city, c.customer_state
accepted.description: Customer table joined to geolocation centroid per zip prefix: one row per customer with representative latitude/longitude (avg) for the customer_zip_code_prefix. Use for customer spatial segmentation and distance-based features. | Use for: Customer geographic segmentation and mapping; Proximity-based marketing and delivery estimations; Aggregating orders by customer region

accepted.name: orders_revenue_joined
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_status,
  o.order_purchase_timestamp,
  COALESCE(item_revenue.total_price, 0.0) AS total_items_price,
  COALESCE(item_revenue.total_freight, 0.0) AS total_freight_value,
  p.payment_lines_count,
  p.payment_value_total
FROM olist_orders o
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(price) AS total_price, SUM(freight_value) AS total_freight
  FROM olist_order_items
  GROUP BY order_id
) item_revenue
  ON o.order_id = item_revenue.order_id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS payment_lines_count, SUM(payment_value) AS payment_value_total
  FROM olist_order_payments
  GROUP BY order_id
) p
  ON o.order_id = p.order_id
accepted.description: Order-level revenue and payment summary joined to order metadata: one row per order with total item revenue, total freight, and payment aggregates. Use for order profitability and revenue analysis. | Use for: Order-level revenue vs payments reconciliation; Identifying orders with missing payment/price records; Profitability and freight cost analysis per order

accepted.name: product_size_volume
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  product_category_name,
  product_name_lenght,
  product_description_lenght,
  product_photos_qty,
  product_weight_g,
  product_length_cm,
  product_height_cm,
  product_width_cm,
  -- compute cubic volume in cubic centimeters when dims available
  (product_length_cm * product_height_cm * product_width_cm) AS product_volume_cm3,
  -- simple size flag: 1 if any dimension or weight present (demonstrative derived column)
  CASE WHEN (product_weight_g IS NOT NULL OR product_length_cm IS NOT NULL OR product_height_cm IS NOT NULL OR product_width_cm IS NOT NULL) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_size_info
FROM olist_products
accepted.description: Per-product physical volume and derived size metrics: one row per product with computed cubic volume and a simple size indicator. Useful for logistics and shipping impact analyses. | Use for: Estimating shipping costs from product volume/weight; Filtering SKUs by available dimension metadata; Category-level average size/weight

accepted.name: orders_rank_by_purchase
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  customer_id,
  order_purchase_timestamp,
  order_status,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_purchase_timestamp DESC) AS customer_order_rank
FROM olist_orders
accepted.description: Rank orders per customer by purchase timestamp (most recent rank 1). One row per order with customer-scoped rank to support top-K queries per customer (e.g., latest N orders). | Use for: Latest orders per customer; Churn detection using recency metrics; Customer lifetime ordering patterns

accepted.name: customer_order_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.customer_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(items.total_price,0.0)) AS total_spent,
  AVG(COALESCE(items.total_price,0.0)) AS avg_order_value,
  AVG(r.review_score) AS avg_review_score
FROM olist_orders o
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(price) AS total_price
  FROM olist_order_items
  GROUP BY order_id
) items
  ON o.order_id = items.order_id
LEFT JOIN olist_order_reviews r
  ON o.order_id = r.order_id
GROUP BY o.customer_id
accepted.description: Aggregated order-level metrics per customer: counts of orders, total spent (from items), average order value and average review score when available. Useful for customer segmentation and LTV proxies. | Use for: Customer lifetime value estimation; Segmentation by spend and satisfaction; Identifying high-value customers
